reviewer: Codex root, second AI-assisted passage comparison

findings.fix: The psalm describes the lawless person in third-person terms; do not call it a first-person description.
findings.before: The no-fear-of-God-before-the-eyes statement corresponds to the psalm’s description of the lawless person. The psalm has his eyes, while Romans has their eyes within its collective chain. The pronoun and surrounding first-person-within-himself description remain distinct.
findings.after: The no-fear-of-God-before-the-eyes statement corresponds to the psalm’s description of the lawless person. The psalm has his eyes, while Romans has their eyes within its collective chain. The singular lawless-person setting and his/their pronoun difference remain distinct.
findings.resolution: Applied the actual singular-setting and pronoun wording after full source/target reading.

findings.fix: State God-of-Gentiles wording directly rather than an ownership-sounding belongs formulation.
findings.before: Paul says God belongs to Gentiles as well as Jews. Peter’s speech rejects divine partiality and accepts those fearing God and practicing righteousness in every nation. The national inclusion corresponds, while Peter’s stated response language and Paul’s faith-justification argument are not collapsed into one quotation.
findings.after: Paul affirms that God is the God of Gentiles as well as Jews. Peter’s speech rejects divine partiality and accepts those fearing God and practicing righteousness in every nation. The national inclusion corresponds, while Peter’s stated response language and Paul’s faith-justification argument are not collapsed into one quotation.
findings.resolution: Applied the scope-of-God wording after reading Romans3:29 and Acts10:34–35.

review_notes: The entire Greek Psalm13:3 chain remains one original unit; quotations preserve different wording and pronouns. Genesis15 uses Abram;17 changes his name to Abraham. Romans4:19 says considered and Genesis17:17 retains laughter without inventing its motive.

James2:21–24 and Romans3:28/4:2 preserve their different actual works/works-of-law and faith formulations without supplying a reconciliation scheme. The circumcision chronology compares Genesis15 and17 as narrative order, not an invented elapsed interval.
